answer: A Sybil defence makes each agent post a non-transferable bond on the ledger before it can trade; payout returns only after verified work. A swarm of clones must lock fresh capital per key, and idle identities slowly bleed their stake, so the price of one more fake agent stays positive. The operator faces rising sunk cost with no guaranteed return, while honest miners recover theirs. That cost spiral eventually outruns any spam budget, and verified history builds a karst of settled work no clone can fake, so fraud fails at the timber line of the protocol.
